ai.description: This 45–55 mm frog is brown with dark dorsal markings and a pale venter. It features prominent, triangular dermal projections above the eyes and a distinct, elongated snout tip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys numhbumaeng* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like dermal projection on each upper eyelid, which is absent or much smaller in similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: The Tamenglong Horned Frog inhabits primary evergreen forests in the Indian subcontinent, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Tamenglong Horned Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush small invertebrate prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys numhbumaeng* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in forest streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Tamenglong Horned Frog is endemic to the Tamenglong district of Manipur, India, where it inhabits high-elevation subtropical evergreen forests.
ai.callDescription: The Tamenglong Horned Frog emits a series of sharp, metallic "tink" notes at a high pitch, typically heard from leaf litter in dense, humid forest habitats.
